clue.text: Woman is head of company across lake

indicators.note: one thing set across another straddles it, so the head of company is spread around the lake

parts.note: chief executive officer, the person at the top of a firm
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A woman runs a company with operations spanning a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of company' tempts you to take just C; it is the whole title CEO, which wraps round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleo is a female first name, short for Cleopatra, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Earlier than second month, returned mineral

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the month's short form is read backwards

parts.note: February is the second month of the year
ore is a mineral mined for its metal

explanation.surface: Something happened earlier than February, when some mineral was sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition 'before' means prior to, earlier in time than something else.

clue.text: Piece of wood on which men carry out checks?

definitions.text: Piece of wood on which men carry out checks?

parts.words: Piece of wood on which men carry out checks?
parts.note: surface reading: a plank on which workers perform inspections
setter's reading: the men are game pieces, and checks are threats to a king, played out on a chequered board

explanation.surface: A wooden plank where workmen carry out inspections.
explanation.walkthrough: Men here are chessmen and a check threatens the king; the board is the piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessboard is the chequered wooden board on which chess pieces are moved and kings are put in check.

clue.text: Went by in a former time, reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is spread by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: the past is a former time; the answer is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Someone went by long ago, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed is the past tense of pass, meaning moved by or went beyond something.

clue.text: Lou has nap cut short — it's most awful!

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the nap word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: Lou's afternoon sleep is interrupted, which is the worst thing ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Lousy is informal for very bad, so the superlative means worst or most awful.

clue.text: A fish in jelly

parts.note: taken as written
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish set in aspic, like jellied eel.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used as a jelly in cooking and laboratories.

clue.text: Social etiquette requiring smart neckwear?

parts.note: nice can mean fine or smart
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Polite society demands a smart necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are the fine points of polite behaviour, the details of social etiquette.

clue.text: Think about keeping chains moving? It's automated

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word for think is read backwards
to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to deem is to think or judge

indicators.note: things moving shift position, so these letters change their order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Consider whether a chain-driven conveyor makes the process automatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think about' reads as consider, but 'about' is the turnaround signal; meed (a reward) is not the meaning here, only the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanised means done by machines rather than by hand, which is to say automated.

clue.text: Scrounger in shelter by church

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
CH is the abbreviation for church; 'by' places it next to the shelter

explanation.surface: A sponger sleeping rough in a shelter beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a parasite, so figuratively a person who lives off others: a scrounger.

clue.text: Adjacent to a pine border

parts.note: taken as written
to pine is to long for something
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Next to a border lined with pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine reads as the tree, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside or next to, exactly what adjacent to says.

clue.text: After arranging, I boost strings initially for these players

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a new order, so the following letters are reordered

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of strings

explanation.surface: An arranger beefs up the string section to suit certain musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboists play the oboe, so they are the players the clue refers to.

clue.text: Rocks on slope caught by start of hurricane, making skidding sound?

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock covering a slope
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: start of points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of hurricane

explanation.surface: Rockfall on a hillside, hit by a storm, sends a car skidding.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a screech is only one kind of skidding noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh high-pitched noise, the kind tyres make when a car skids.

clue.text: American nerd's wife in river? Bravo!

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, so the wife's letter goes within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American geek cheers his wife on as she swims in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife's W goes inside DEE, then B is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a boring, socially awkward person, a nerd.

clue.text: Some seen in court protect workers

parts.note: to defend is to protect
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: People in court are there to protect workers' rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Defendants are the accused parties in a trial, so they are among those present in court.

clue.text: Stop working with old Venetian painter's medical advisor

parts.note: a machine that dies stops working
Titian was the sixteenth-century Venetian master

explanation.surface: An Old Master's doctor tells him to stop working.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian is a health professional who gives expert advice on diet and nutrition.

clue.text: Not well, say again: poorly educated

parts.note: ill means unwell
to iterate is to repeat or say again

explanation.surface: A doctor's note about an unwell patient who has had little schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiterate means unable to read and write, so lacking education.

clue.text: Students with final MA turning into extremists

indicators.note: turning means changing round, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Graduates taking their last master's exam become radicalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentalists hold strict literal beliefs and are often extreme in their views.

clue.text: Snuggling up with young flier

definitions.meaning: first meaning: settling cosily against something
second meaning: a baby bird still in its nest

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense and the noun sense are spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to snuggle, and a nestling is a chick too young to leave the nest.

clue.text: Almost begrudge actor Jeremy's surroundings

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the begrudge word is dropped

parts.note: to envy is to begrudge
Jeremy Irons is an English actor

explanation.surface: Someone nearly resents where the actor Jeremy Irons lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Environs are the surrounding area of a place, its neighbourhood.

clue.text: Struggling Devon side declined rapidly

indicators.note: a struggling team is in disarray, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A struggling team from Devon, the English county, slid down the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To nosedive is to plunge steeply, as a plane does, hence to fall or decline sharply.

clue.text: Really like established periodical

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A fan really enjoys a long-running magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a magazine summarising articles, such as Reader's Digest, so a periodical.

clue.text: Carried as far as Edward

parts.note: to can mean up to or as far as
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone carried a load all the way to Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, so toted means carried.

clue.text: Hurried through ground etc in dream-like state

indicators.note: passing through something means being inside it, so the hurried word sits within the other
ground means crushed and broken up, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: to hurry is to run, so hurried is ran
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rushed across the field and so on, as if half asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun for land; here it is the past of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a half-conscious state like sleepwalking or dreaming.

clue.text: Everything's by pitch, perhaps involving the best players?

parts.note: everything is all, with the 's kept
pitch is one kind of tar, hence 'perhaps'; 'by' places it next

explanation.surface: Everything happens beside the playing field when the top players appear.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks like a sports field, fitting the surface, but it is the black sticky substance.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star team or cast is made up entirely of the top performers.

clue.text: Tito memoir includes this volume

indicators.note: includes says the phrase holds the answer within its run of letters

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: The Yugoslav leader's autobiography contains this book.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a book, especially a large heavy one, so a volume.

clue.text: Clothes grow old? Rubbish!

parts.note: garb is clothing
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that clothes wear out with time.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage means refuse, and as an exclamation it means nonsense, like 'Rubbish!'.

clue.text: Otherwise included in rising prices ledger

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the run of letters goes backwards
included in says the letters sit inside the following phrase

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An accounts book records that prices are going up, or not.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or else you'll miss it'.

clue.text: European chaps in temporary accommodation — some flats?

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the temporary accommodation

parts.note: tents are shelters put up for a short stay
E is the abbreviation for European
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Visiting European men camp out in what might be called apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the answer as an example: tenement blocks are divided into flats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenements are large buildings split into rented flats, so they are examples of flats.

clue.text: Fixes duty, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken form, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a duty is a tax levied on goods; the answer sounds the same

explanation.surface: Someone sets the import duty, by the sound of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack is to fasten with small nails or stitches, so tacks means fixes.
